detail:
A National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) advanced-reading handout on gout, preserved on the Federal Depository Library Program archive, summarizes what research has established about the disease and where investigation continues. The handout describes how studies of uric acid metabolism clarified why some people overproduce uric acid while others excrete too little, and how genetic and kidney-function research has helped explain differences in susceptibility.

The handout also describes research into the inflammatory process itself: how urate crystals activate immune pathways in the joint, why flares eventually subside on their own, and how imaging and laboratory methods have improved the detection of crystal deposits, including deposits present between flares. NIAMS presents these lines of work as the basis for current treatment classes and for ongoing studies of inflammation in gout, rather than as findings that change day-to-day care on their own.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about gout research.

title: Gout: what research explains about urate crystals and inflammation
